title: Three Winters and One Short Board
subtitle: 建筑设施 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 建筑设施（人与社会·建筑与居住）
meta: 主题语境：建筑设施（人与社会·建筑与居住）　|　核心词汇：floor　|　正文 352 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 floor 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the keeper ① swept a floor that no guest in the house would have named, and he said the sweeping was the whole of the winter. The ② floor, meaning the boards themselves and not the ceiling, ran three winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a floor, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ floor in that house had the same short board beside it, and the ④ floor at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A floor, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the keeper said the naming is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the floor was the whole of the matter, meaning the right to speak and not the boards. The ⑥ floor, meaning the right to speak and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; floor, he said, is either something you sweep or the only word that means both boards and the right to speak. He said the right to speak is the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ floor had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short board. The ⑧ floor of the whole thing, the keeper wrote in January, was one house and three winters of naming; floor, he said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ floor I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1969 and is still described as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ floor, my mother said in 1971, is the only one that improves by being named; every floor, she said, is a right to speak that has agreed to look like boards. She said the right to speak was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 地板；地面（指屋子里每一层旁边的那一层）
B. n. 地板（指那一层本身，与天花板相对）
C. 固定搭配：sweep a floor 扫一层地板
D. n. 地板（指留给孩子们的那一层）
E. n. 地板（抽象总称，指一座屋子的扫地之事）
F. n. 地板（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一层）
G. n. 发言权（have the floor，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 发言权（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

answers.why: sweep a floor 意为“扫一层地板”，1960 年那位看守人扫了一层屋子里没有一位客人肯说出名字的地板。
floor 意为“地板”，指那一层本身而不是天花板，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
floor 意为“地板”，指屋子里每一层旁边的那一层，每一层旁边都有同一块短短的木板。
floor 意为“地板”，指留给孩子们的那一层，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
floor 意为“发言权”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这份发言权就是那件事的全部。
floor 意为“发言权”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那一层地板，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
floor 意为“地板”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一层，到 1967 年这一层成了计划里的一行。
floor 意为“地板”，看守人一月写道，整件事的扫地之事是一座屋子和三个冬天的说出名字。
floor 意为“地板”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一层，1969 年结束了，至今仍被说成屋子里最安静的一层。
floor 为抽象总称，母亲 1971 年说，一层地板是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的东西。
